problems.title: Unknown USB Device (Device Descriptor Request Failed) Code 43
problems.body: My USB drive is not recognized. Device Manager shows 'Unknown USB Device (Device Descriptor Request Failed)' with 'Windows has stopped this device because it has reported problems. (Code 43)'.

solutions.body: Fully power-drain the laptop: shut down, unplug the charger and all USB devices, hold the power button for 30 seconds, then boot and reconnect.
Disable USB selective suspend: Control Panel > Power Options > Change plan settings > Advanced > USB settings > USB selective suspend > Disabled.

problems.title: External monitor not detected through laptop USB-C port
problems.body: I connected a USB-C to HDMI adapter to my laptop's USB-C port, but the monitor says 'No signal' and Windows doesn't detect it.

solutions.body: Use a USB-C port that supports DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt (look for the DP or lightning-bolt icon next to the port), and update the graphics driver.

problems.title: MacBook Air only drives one external monitor
problems.body: I connected two monitors to my MacBook Air through a dock but only one ever lights up.

solutions.body: Base M1/M2 chips support only one external display natively. Use a DisplayLink dock or adapter and install the DisplayLink Manager app for the second monitor.
Close the lid (clamshell mode) with power connected; the MacBook then drives two external displays.

problems.title: Windows 11: 'Your PIN is no longer available due to a change to the security settings on this device'
problems.body: After an update, the sign-in screen says 'Your PIN is no longer available due to a change to the security settings on this device' and offers to set up the PIN again, which fails.

solutions.body: Sign in with your account password, then reset the Windows Hello container by deleting the Ngc folder and setting up a new PIN.
steps: Sign in with the account password (Sign-in options > key icon)
As administrator, take ownership of and delete C:\Windows\ServiceProfiles\LocalService\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Ngc
Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options > PIN > Set up

problems.title: Laptop battery says 'Plugged in, not charging' at 60-80%
problems.body: My laptop stops charging at around 60% and shows 'Plugged in, not charging'. The battery is less than a year old.

solutions.body: A battery conservation threshold is enabled. In Lenovo Vantage > Power > Battery settings, turn off Conservation Mode (or change the custom charge threshold).

problems.title: Windows Update KB5034441 fails with error 0x80070643
problems.body: The security update KB5034441 keeps failing with 0x80070643 in Windows Update on Windows 10 22H2.

solutions.body: The WinRE recovery partition is too small. Shrink the OS partition and enlarge the recovery partition by 250 MB following Microsoft's manual steps for KB5034441, then retry the update.

problems.title: Wi-Fi option disappeared from Windows 11 settings
problems.body: After a Windows update, the Wi-Fi tile and Wi-Fi section in Settings are gone; only Ethernet appears.

solutions.body: Run Network reset: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset > Reset now, then restart.
Uninstall the Wi-Fi adapter in Device Manager (tick 'delete driver' if offered), restart, and install the vendor's driver.

problems.title: Keyboard types the wrong symbols (@ and " swapped)
problems.body: When I press Shift+2 I get " instead of @, and some other symbols are in the wrong place.

solutions.body: Windows switched to a different keyboard layout (e.g. UK instead of US). Remove the extra layout in Settings > Time & language > Language & region > language options > Keyboards, or switch with Win+Space.

problems.title: MacBook shows 'Battery is not charging' while plugged in
problems.body: My MacBook's battery menu says 'Battery Is Not Charging' even though the charger is connected and the battery is at 50%.

solutions.body: Reset the SMC: shut down, hold left Shift + left Control + left Option + power for 10 seconds, release, and start up.
If Optimized Battery Charging is on, macOS deliberately pauses at 80%. Choose 'Charge to Full Now' from the battery menu.

problems.title: BitLocker recovery screen after BIOS update
problems.body: After a BIOS update my laptop boots into a blue 'BitLocker recovery' screen asking for a 48-digit recovery key.

solutions.body: Find the key in your Microsoft account (account.microsoft.com > Devices > Manage recovery keys) from another device, match the Key ID shown on screen, and enter it.

problems.title: Bluetooth missing from Windows 11 Settings and Device Manager
problems.body: The Bluetooth toggle vanished from Quick Settings and the Bluetooth category is missing in Device Manager.

solutions.body: Power-drain the laptop: shut down, unplug the charger, hold power for 30 seconds, then boot. The combo Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip re-enumerates.
Install the Bluetooth driver from the laptop manufacturer's support page.

problems.title: Xbox controller won't pair over Bluetooth with computer
problems.body: My Xbox Wireless Controller shows up in Bluetooth settings but fails to pair or disconnects immediately.

solutions.body: Update the controller firmware with the Xbox Accessories app (connect via USB cable, open the app, choose Update), then pair again.

problems.title: Windows: Wi-Fi 'Connected, no internet'
problems.body: My Windows laptop shows 'No internet, secured' on Wi-Fi while other devices work fine on the same network.

solutions.body: Reset the IP configuration, DNS cache, and Winsock catalog from an elevated Command Prompt, then restart.
solutions.code:
ipconfig /release
ipconfig /renew
ipconfig /flushdns
netsh winsock reset
netsh int ip reset

problems.title: Smart plug can't connect to mesh Wi-Fi during setup
problems.body: My new smart plug fails at the 'connecting to Wi-Fi' step every time. My mesh network uses one name for 2.4 and 5 GHz.

solutions.body: Most smart plugs only support 2.4 GHz. Temporarily disable 5 GHz (or create a separate 2.4 GHz SSID/IoT network) during setup, and keep the phone near the plug.

problems.title: Nintendo Switch NAT type D / error 2618-0516 in online games
problems.body: Online matches fail with 'Error Code: 2618-0516' and the connection test shows NAT Type D.

solutions.body: Enable UPnP on the router, restart the Switch, and rerun the connection test.
Give the Switch a static IP and forward UDP ports 1-65535 to it (or put it in the router's DMZ).

problems.title: PS5 downloads are very slow on Wi-Fi
problems.body: Game downloads on my PS5 crawl at a few MB/s even though my connection is 500 Mbps.

solutions.body: Connect the PS5 with an Ethernet cable.
Set DNS manually to 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 in Settings > Network > Set Up Internet Connection > Advanced Settings.

problems.title: Double NAT with ISP modem-router and my own router
problems.body: My own Wi-Fi router is connected to the ISP's modem-router. Port forwarding doesn't work and consoles report strict NAT.

solutions.body: Put the ISP modem-router into bridge (modem-only) mode so only your router does NAT, then restart both.

problems.title: Android: Wi-Fi says 'Connected without internet'
problems.body: My Android phone shows 'Connected without internet' on my home Wi-Fi; laptops work fine.

solutions.body: A custom Private DNS host is unreachable. Set Settings > Network & internet > Private DNS to Automatic or Off.

problems.title: iPhone shows 'Weak Security' warning for home Wi-Fi
problems.body: Under my Wi-Fi network name the iPhone says 'Weak Security: WPA/WPA2 (TKIP) is not considered secure'.

solutions.body: In the router's wireless security settings choose WPA2-Personal (AES) or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode instead of WPA/WPA2 TKIP.

problems.title: Chromecast (2nd gen) shows 'Untrusted device' and can't cast
problems.body: Since early March 2025 my Chromecast 2nd gen can't be cast to; the Google Home app says it's an untrusted device or can't be verified.

solutions.body: Factory reset the Chromecast by holding its button for 25 seconds.
Don't factory reset. Keep the device powered on and connected; Google pushed a firmware update that restores casting. If you already reset it, update the Google Home app and set it up again.

problems.title: Windows 11 can't access NAS share: organization's security policies block unauthenticated guest access
problems.body: Opening \\nas\share fails: 'You can't access this shared folder because your organization's security policies block unauthenticated guest access.'

solutions.body: Enable insecure guest logons: gpedit.msc > Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Network > Lanman Workstation > 'Enable insecure guest logons' > Enabled.
Create a user account with a password on the NAS and connect with those credentials instead of guest access.

problems.title: Ethernet link stuck at 100 Mbps instead of 1 Gbps
problems.body: My PC's network adapter shows a link speed of 100 Mbps although the router and the PC are gigabit.

solutions.body: Gigabit needs all four wire pairs. Replace the cable with a known-good Cat5e/Cat6 cable; check for bent pins on the plugs.

problems.title: Netflix error NW-2-5 on smart TV
problems.body: Netflix on my smart TV shows 'Netflix has encountered an error. Code: NW-2-5'. Other apps work intermittently.

solutions.body: Restart the TV and router, and set the TV's DNS to automatic. If on Wi-Fi, try Ethernet.
